name: Narrowcast
description: Narrowcast is a selective attentional modulator that interfaces with BCI-adjacent neural pathways to suppress processing of non-threat stimuli while amplifying sensory channels relevant to immediate danger — motion, sound directionality, peripheral movement, and target acquisition. The world does not slow down on Narrowcast, but irrelevant information simply stops registering, creating a state of pure combat cognition stripped of distraction. Originally developed as a focus aid for air traffic and industrial safety, its combat applications were immediately apparent.
effects: Suppression of non-combat sensory and cognitive processing
Enhanced spatial awareness of immediate combat environment
Elimination of distraction from environmental noise, emotion, and peripheral stimuli
side_effects: Blindness to non-threat information — civilian bystanders, escape routes, and allies may not register
Complete inability to perform complex cognitive tasks outside threat-response during duration
Social and communicative function severely impaired — verbal coordination with teammates becomes difficult
Post-duration overstimulation as suppressed sensory input floods back
Dangerous interaction with BCI hardware — some implant configurations cause feedback loops
Rare cases of users unable to deactivate threat-classification mode without medical intervention
cultural_context: Narrowcast requires a BCI to function, which limits it to Tier 2 and above — getting a neural direct interface is expensive enough that Shelf runners rarely have the hardware. Among professional mercenary teams it's considered the most tactically sophisticated combat drug available: it makes you better at fighting without making you faster or stronger, which means a skilled user becomes genuinely dangerous. The dark reputation comes from its side effect profile — several friendly-fire incidents in corporate security operations have been attributed to Narrowcast users who simply stopped registering their teammates as distinct from obstacles.
story_hooks: A runner wakes up after a Narrowcast op with no memory of a 12-minute window in which, according to witnesses, they killed two people who were not threats — and the neural cartridge's log data has been wiped.
A Helix engineer contacts a fixer claiming the current Narrowcast formulation has a known defect that the company buried — under certain BCI configurations, it doesn't shut off.

A team of professional mercs all using Narrowcast simultaneously can't coordinate at all — they've hired a runner who isn't using it to act as human comms relay between four highly capable but completely isolated fighters.
